skills: Define the AWS shared responsibility model
questions.question: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which of the following is the customer's responsibility?

choices.text: Patching the hypervisor software on Amazon EC2 host servers.
choices.explanation: AWS is responsible for maintaining and patching the infrastructure that runs AWS services, including hypervisors.

choices.text: Configuring security group rules and network ACLs for an Amazon VPC.
choices.explanation: Security groups and network ACLs are customer-managed controls. Customers are responsible for configuring these firewall rules to control traffic to and from their resources.

choices.text: Maintaining the physical security of AWS data centres.
choices.explanation: Physical security of data centres is entirely AWS's responsibility under the shared responsibility model.

choices.text: Replacing failed hard drives on Amazon S3 storage servers.
choices.explanation: Hardware maintenance, including storage device replacement, is an AWS responsibility as part of the 'security of the cloud' domain.

questions.tip: Think about what falls under 'security IN the cloud' (customer) versus 'security OF the cloud' (AWS).
questions.explanation: The AWS Shared Responsibility Model divides security duties: AWS handles 'security of the cloud' (hardware, networking, facilities, hypervisor), while customers handle 'security in the cloud' (data, IAM, OS patching on EC2, firewall/network configuration, encryption). Configuring security groups and NACLs is a core customer responsibility — these are the virtual firewalls that customers must set up correctly to protect their workloads.
